mechanism_narrative: The significant week-on-week rebound in RETAIL_REC mobility observed at t-0w indicates a renewed public willingness to engage in out-of-home activities, which will sustain and further improve retail and recreation footfall over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the average of the last 28 days, indicating the t-0w rebound was an anomaly.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained return to workplaces, evidenced by WORKPLACES mobility rising for two consecutive weeks, will drive increased weekday foot traffic to nearby retail and recreation establishments, leading to higher RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next two weeks despite WORKPLACES rising for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: As RESIDENTIAL mobility declines and WORKPLACES mobility simultaneously increases, it signals a shift in daily routines where people are spending less time at home and more time in public and commercial spaces, directly boosting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls by more than 2 points while WORKPLACES rises by more than 2 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC decreases over the next 28 days despite a concurrent fall in RESIDENTIAL and rise in WORKPLACES.

mechanism_narrative: The broad-based recovery observed across RETAIL_REC, PARKS, TRANSIT, and WORKPLACES in t-0w indicates an underlying easing of public health restrictions or a significant shift in public sentiment, which will continue to drive RETAIL_REC upwards over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: The average RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the average of the last 28 days, despite the broad recovery observed at t-0w.

mechanism_narrative: Despite the t-0w rebound, RETAIL_REC remains significantly below baseline. If this rebound is not sustained and RETAIL_REC falls again in the immediate next week, it indicates a fragile recovery and will lead to lower RETAIL_REC over the next week.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next week, even if it falls in t+1w, suggesting the initial drop was a temporary fluctuation.

mechanism_narrative: Persistent low TRANSIT mobility, remaining below -60% for two consecutive weeks, indicates a continued reluctance or inability to use public transport, which will significantly hinder the recovery of RETAIL_REC, particularly in areas reliant on public transit, leading to lower RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -60% for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days despite TRANSIT remaining below -60% for two consecutive weeks, suggesting other transport modes compensate.

mechanism_narrative: The rebound in PARKS mobility at t-0w suggests an increase in general outdoor activity and public comfort, which often precedes or coincides with increased engagement in other out-of-home activities, including retail and recreation, leading to higher RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC decreases over the next two weeks despite PARKS mobility showing a sustained increase.

mechanism_narrative: The consistent stability of GROCERY_PHARM mobility near baseline, coupled with the recent decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility, indicates that essential activities are maintained while people are increasingly venturing out, providing a stable foundation for RETAIL_REC to increase over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM remains within +/- 5% of baseline for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC decreases over the next 28 days even if GROCERY_PHARM remains stable and RESIDENTIAL declines.
